correctness.rationale: For every distinct a,b in a connected set, point separation supplies a scalar functional separating them. Continuity converts it to a 1/p-Hölder map for d_p. Its connected image contains a nondegenerate real interval, so the direct Hausdorff-cover inequality forces dim_H K >= 1/p. Affine segments are scaled copies of ([0,1],|s-t|^p), giving equality. In L_p[0,1], the indicator path is exactly isometric to [0,1] for d_p, and the universal dimension-at-least-one bound for nondegenerate connected metric spaces yields minimum 1. All quantifiers and boundary assumptions are explicit; no computation or enumeration substitutes for proof.

value.rationale: The result identifies a natural exact invariant: the minimum Hausdorff dimension of a nondegenerate connected subset in the canonical metric of a point-separating p-Banach space. It upgrades qualitative curve rigidity to a sharp quantitative barrier for all connected sets, has explicit extremizers, and pinpoints the necessity of point separation by an exact drop from 1/p to 1 in the canonical L_p example.
